title: It's been awhile but my game has evolved into an Anime RTS looter from it's early version of a turn-based Anime looter
author: RuinousFate
selftext:
This is now the third battle system I've implemented and I'm honestly pretty happy with it!

  
First version was turn-based and biggest feedback was it was too simple (but that it being fast was great)

  
Second version was a grid-based version but the feedback became that it was too slow (battles took 2 minutes)

  
This third version merges the best of both worlds, positioning can matter and you have individual control of how to move characters... Though I guess I didn't really showcase that in the video but you can use the D-pad/joystick to manually move a character. Plus, it also supports battles against a large number of enemies (20+!) vs my old system that could do only 5.

  
This has also incorporated one of my favorite fantasy mechanics which is Essences from STGAAB.

  
 My next goals will be balance changes as well as AI behavior improvements and the ability to set behaviors like in Unicorn Overlord.

comments.body: Very nice!! Love the VFX and animation what was your workflow for such smoothness

replies.author: RuinousFate
replies.body:
I tried it with Codex SOL and it was terrible ngl

Astra was the game changer. Still took a lot of prompting to get a VFX to a standard I liked and then I built off of that. You just need one good success to build your next one. I would go hard with that one success, multiple layers, Astra Ultra, etc. After one success, you can create another and before you know, you have a good standard for what is good VFX for it to build off of.

Mind you I burned a whole week of Astra $200 usage to get my VFX library solid but well worth it. Still falls back to not quite solid VFX now and then though smh.

replies.author: RuinousFate
replies.body:
I haven't tried the services for VFX personally. You can buy some cheap VFX asset packs to get you started though. 

For the prompts, reference images helped or YouTube videos even. For me what helped was that I had a good idea of exactly what effect I wanted as my "first"
